prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: a declined claim the member disputes. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a claim is declined for lack of proof, I should check whether the member has given a clear timeline, photos, repair invoices or a crime reference before treating it as a firm refusal."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the policy wording turns on an exclusion, I should state the exact clause in plain English and link it to the reported circumstances, so the member can see why the decline was reached."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member disputes the date of loss, I should compare the loss description with weather data, call logs and repair timing rather than relying on a single note on the file."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the evidence is borderline, I prefer to pause and gather one more independent source, because a well-supported decision is easier to defend than a quick decline."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a previous repair or maintenance issue is mentioned, I should separate wear and tear from sudden damage and avoid assuming the whole claim falls to a maintenance problem."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the dispute is about storm, flood or escape of water, I should check whether the cause of damage is the peril itself or a pre-existing defect that merely became visible at the same time."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member says the loss is covered but the claim was declined on valuation grounds, I should verify whether the disagreement is really about cover, settlement amount or betterment."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I am uncertain whether the matter is within delegated authority, I prefer to escalate early rather than continue arguing a point that may need specialist review."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member has not understood the decline, I should summarise the decision in short steps: what was reported, what was checked, what the policy requires and where the gap lies."},{"type":"fact","content":"When new evidence could change the outcome, I should reopen the triage with that evidence in mind, because a declined claim should stay open to correction if the facts support it."}]}
